claim: Loss-of-function of MeCP2 causes Rett syndrome (RTT).
source: Loss- and gain-of-function of MeCP2 causes Rett syndrome (RTT) and MECP2 duplication syndrome (MDS), respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citation to established scientific knowledge about MECP2 mutations.

claim: Gain-of-function of MeCP2 causes MECP2 duplication syndrome (MDS).
source: Loss- and gain-of-function of MeCP2 causes Rett syndrome (RTT) and MECP2 duplication syndrome (MDS), respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citation to established scientific knowledge about MECP2 mutations.

claim: MeCP2 binds methyl-cytosines to finely tune gene expression in the brain.
source: MeCP2 binds methyl-cytosines to finely tune gene expression in the brain, but identifying genes robustly regulated by MeCP2 has been difficult.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction to prior work on MeCP2 function.

claim: Gdf11 is down-regulated in RTT mouse models.
source: Gdf11 is down-regulated in RTT mouse models and, conversely, up-regulated in MDS mouse models.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in Figure 1B showing Gdf11 expression changes across multiple RTT mouse models.

claim: Gdf11 is up-regulated in MDS mouse models.
source: Gdf11 is down-regulated in RTT mouse models and, conversely, up-regulated in MDS mouse models.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in Figure 1B showing Gdf11 expression changes across multiple MDS mouse models.

claim: Genetically normalizing Gdf11 dosage levels improved several behavioral deficits in a mouse model of MDS.
source: Strikingly, genetically normalizing Gdf11 dosage levels improved several behavioral deficits in a mouse model of MDS.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data presented in Figure 2 showing improvements in locomotion, activity, and learning in MECP2-TG1; Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.

claim: Losing one copy of Gdf11 alone was sufficient to cause multiple neurobehavioral deficits in mice.
source: Next, we discovered that losing one copy of Gdf11 alone was sufficient to cause multiple neurobehavioral deficits in mice, most notably hyperactivity and decreased learning and memory.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data presented in Figure 3 showing hyperactivity and learning/memory deficits in Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.

claim: Loss of one copy of Gdf11 causes hyperactivity in mice.
source: Next, we discovered that losing one copy of Gdf11 alone was sufficient to cause multiple neurobehavioral deficits in mice, most notably hyperactivity and decreased learning and memory.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3A showing increased distance traveled and activity counts in Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.

claim: Loss of one copy of Gdf11 causes decreased learning and memory in mice.
source: Next, we discovered that losing one copy of Gdf11 alone was sufficient to cause multiple neurobehavioral deficits in mice, most notably hyperactivity and decreased learning and memory.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3E showing reduced freezing in contextual and cued fear conditioning in Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.

claim: The decrease in learning and memory in Gdf11tm2b/+ mice was not due to changes in proliferation or numbers of progenitor cells in the hippocampus.
source: This decrease in learning and memory was not due to changes in proliferation or numbers of progenitor cells in the hippocampus.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4 showing no significant changes in EdU+, SOX2+, or GFAP+ cells in the dentate gyrus of Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.

claim: Loss of one copy of Gdf11 decreased survival in mice.
source: Lastly, loss of one copy of Gdf11 decreased survival in mice, corroborating its putative role in aging.
evidence: This is supported by survival data in Figure 3F showing reduced median survival in Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.

claim: Gdf11 dosage is important for brain function.
source: Our data demonstrate that Gdf11 dosage is important for brain function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the behavioral data showing that both reduction and normalization of Gdf11 dosage affect neurological phenotypes.

claim: Intellectual disability (ID) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affect nearly 3% of children in the United States.
source: Intellectual disability (ID) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affect nearly 3% of children in the United States (Zablotsky et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zablotsky et al., 2019.

claim: ID and ASD can be caused by mutations in any one of hundreds of genes.
source: These diseases can be caused by mutations in any one of hundreds of genes (Deciphering Developmental Disorders Study, 2017; Satterstrom et al., 2020), a subset of which is 'dosage-sensitive', causing neurological dysfunction by either loss-of-function mutations or an increase in expression due to copy-number gain (Rice and McLysaght, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Deciphering Developmental Disorders Study, 2017 and Satterstrom et al., 2020.

claim: A subset of genes causing ID and ASD is 'dosage-sensitive', causing neurological dysfunction by either loss-of-function mutations or an increase in expression due to copy-number gain.
source: These diseases can be caused by mutations in any one of hundreds of genes (Deciphering Developmental Disorders Study, 2017; Satterstrom et al., 2020), a subset of which is 'dosage-sensitive', causing neurological dysfunction by either loss-of-function mutations or an increase in expression due to copy-number gain (Rice and McLysaght, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rice and McLysaght, 2017.

claim: MECP2 is an X-linked gene whose loss-of-function causes Rett syndrome (RTT; OMIM: 312750).
source: MECP2 is an X-linked gene whose loss-of-function causes Rett syndrome (RTT; OMIM: 312750) (Amir et al., 1999) and whose duplication causes MECP2 duplication syndrome (MDS; OMIM: 300260) (Lugtenberg et al., 2009; van Esch et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Amir et al., 1999.

claim: MECP2 duplication causes MECP2 duplication syndrome (MDS; OMIM: 300260).
source: MECP2 is an X-linked gene whose loss-of-function causes Rett syndrome (RTT; OMIM: 312750) (Amir et al., 1999) and whose duplication causes MECP2 duplication syndrome (MDS; OMIM: 300260) (Lugtenberg et al., 2009; van Esch et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lugtenberg et al., 2009 and van Esch et al., 2005.

claim: RTT and MDS are devastating neurological disorders characterized by intellectual disability, motor dysfunction, and seizures.
source: Both RTT and MDS are devastating neurological disorders characterized by intellectual disability, motor dysfunction, and seizures.
evidence: This is based on established clinical knowledge about RTT and MDS.

claim: MeCP2 is a methyl-cytosine binding protein that regulates gene expression in the brain.
source: MeCP2 is a methyl-cytosine binding protein that regulates gene expression in the brain (Chen et al., 2015; Gabel et al., 2015; Nan et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2015; Gabel et al., 2015; and Nan et al., 1997.

claim: Disruption of normal MeCP2 function causes subtle dysregulation of thousands of genes.
source: Disruption of normal MeCP2 function causes subtle dysregulation of thousands of genes (Sanfeliu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sanfeliu et al., 2019.

claim: Many dysregulated genes are shared between mouse models of RTT and MDS, but their expression is altered in opposite directions.
source: Importantly, many of these dysregulated genes are shared between mouse models of RTT and MDS, but their expression is altered in opposite directions (Chahrour et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chahrour et al., 2008 and Chen et al., 2015.

claim: Gdf11 is a secreted ligand of the TGFβ superfamily most closely related to myostatin/GDF8.
source: Gdf11 is a secreted ligand of the TGFβ superfamily most closely related to myostatin/GDF8 (Morikawa et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Morikawa et al., 2016.

claim: Gdf11 was first identified as a regulator of the anterior/posterior patterning of the skeleton.
source: Gdf11 was first identified as a regulator of the anterior/posterior patterning of the skeleton (McPherron et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to McPherron et al., 1999.

claim: Gdf11 negatively regulates neurogenesis both during development and in the adult brain.
source: Further studies have revealed that Gdf11 negatively regulates neurogenesis both during development and in the adult brain (Mayweather et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mayweather et al., 2021 and Wu et al., 2003.

claim: Gdf11 has been implicated as a 'rejuvenating' factor that mitigates the effects of aging.
source: Gdf11 has also been implicated as a 'rejuvenating' factor that mitigates the effects of aging and as a tumor suppressor in multiple organs (Bajikar et al., 2017; Katsimpardi et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Loffredo et al., 2013; Sinha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Katsimpardi et al., 2014; Loffredo et al., 2013; and Sinha et al., 2014.

claim: Gdf11 has been implicated as a tumor suppressor in multiple organs.
source: Gdf11 has also been implicated as a 'rejuvenating' factor that mitigates the effects of aging and as a tumor suppressor in multiple organs (Bajikar et al., 2017; Katsimpardi et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Loffredo et al., 2013; Sinha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bajikar et al., 2017 and Liu et al., 2018.

claim: Mutations in GDF11 have been associated with a developmental disorder with craniofacial, vertebral, and neurological abnormalities.
source: Recently, mutations in GDF11 have been associated with a developmental disorder with craniofacial, vertebral, and neurological abnormalities, but the consequences of altered Gdf11 dosage on mouse behavior had not been previously assessed (Cox et al., 2019; Ravenscroft et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cox et al., 2019 and Ravenscroft et al., 2021.

claim: The consequences of altered Gdf11 dosage on mouse behavior had not been previously assessed prior to this study.
source: Recently, mutations in GDF11 have been associated with a developmental disorder with craniofacial, vertebral, and neurological abnormalities, but the consequences of altered Gdf11 dosage on mouse behavior had not been previously assessed (Cox et al., 2019; Ravenscroft et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated explicitly in the introduction.

claim: Normalizing MeCP2 levels through genetic or pharmacological means is sufficient to rescue nearly all behavioral and molecular deficits in a mouse model of MDS.
source: Normalizing MeCP2 levels through genetic or pharmacological means is sufficient to rescue nearly all behavioral and molecular deficits in a mouse model of MDS (Sztainberg et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sztainberg et al., 2015.

claim: Bolus injection of an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) targeting MECP2 acutely reduces MeCP2 protein in MDS mice and ameliorates behavioral deficits.
source: For example, bolus injection of an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) targeting MECP2 acutely reduces MeCP2 protein in MDS mice and ameliorates behavioral deficits (Shao et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2021b.

claim: 16 genes had fold-changes highly correlated (Spearman's rho >±0.75) with MeCP2 levels.
source: We found 16 genes whose fold-changes were highly correlated (Spearman's rho >±0.75) with MeCP2 levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Four genes (Gdf11, Fam131b, Vcan, and Foxp1) were identified with a probability of loss intolerance (pLI) greater than 0.9 among the 16 MeCP2-correlated genes.
source: Of the 16 MeCP2-correlated genes, we identified four genes – growth differentiation factor 11 (Gdf11), family with sequence similarity 131 member B (Fam131b), versican (Vcan), and forkhead box protein P1 (Foxp1) with a probability of loss intolerance (pLI) greater than 0.9 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Gdf11 was significantly altered in 19 of the 20 transcriptional profiles from MECP2 perturbed brain samples.
source: Strikingly, we found that Gdf11 was significantly altered in 19 of the 20 profiles, whereas the other three genes did not consistently exhibit significant difference compared to control (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: GDF11 levels were downregulated two-fold in human postmortem RTT excitatory neurons.
source: GDF11 levels were downregulated two-fold in human postmortem RTT excitatory neurons, while Gdf11 levels were downregulated in the transcriptomes of Mecp2-null male mice, Mecp2-null heterozygous female mice (Pohodich et al., 2018), and a panel of MECP2 point mutant male mice in multiple brain regions (Jiang et al., 2021; Boxer et al., 2020; Baker et al., 2013); these data suggest Gdf11 is robustly sensitive to MeCP2 function.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and citations to the original studies.

claim: Gdf11 levels were downregulated in the transcriptomes of Mecp2-null male mice.
source: GDF11 levels were downregulated two-fold in human postmortem RTT excitatory neurons, while Gdf11 levels were downregulated in the transcriptomes of Mecp2-null male mice, Mecp2-null heterozygous female mice (Pohodich et al., 2018), and a panel of MECP2 point mutant male mice in multiple brain regions (Jiang et al., 2021; Boxer et al., 2020; Baker et al., 2013); these data suggest Gdf11 is robustly sensitive to MeCP2 function.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Gdf11 levels were downregulated in Mecp2-null heterozygous female mice.
source: GDF11 levels were downregulated two-fold in human postmortem RTT excitatory neurons, while Gdf11 levels were downregulated in the transcriptomes of Mecp2-null male mice, Mecp2-null heterozygous female mice (Pohodich et al., 2018), and a panel of MECP2 point mutant male mice in multiple brain regions (Jiang et al., 2021; Boxer et al., 2020; Baker et al., 2013); these data suggest Gdf11 is robustly sensitive to MeCP2 function.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pohodich et al., 2018 and data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Gdf11 levels were downregulated in a panel of MECP2 point mutant male mice in multiple brain regions.
source: GDF11 levels were downregulated two-fold in human postmortem RTT excitatory neurons, while Gdf11 levels were downregulated in the transcriptomes of Mecp2-null male mice, Mecp2-null heterozygous female mice (Pohodich et al., 2018), and a panel of MECP2 point mutant male mice in multiple brain regions (Jiang et al., 2021; Boxer et al., 2020; Baker et al., 2013); these data suggest Gdf11 is robustly sensitive to MeCP2 function.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2021; Boxer et al., 2020; and Baker et al., 2013, and data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Gdf11 is robustly sensitive to MeCP2 function.
source: GDF11 levels were downregulated two-fold in human postmortem RTT excitatory neurons, while Gdf11 levels were downregulated in the transcriptomes of Mecp2-null male mice, Mecp2-null heterozygous female mice (Pohodich et al., 2018), and a panel of MECP2 point mutant male mice in multiple brain regions (Jiang et al., 2021; Boxer et al., 2020; Baker et al., 2013); these data suggest Gdf11 is robustly sensitive to MeCP2 function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the consistent downregulation of Gdf11 across multiple RTT models.

claim: Gdf11 was significantly upregulated in mouse models overexpressing MECP2.
source: Additionally, we also found that Gdf11 was significantly upregulated in mouse models overexpressing MECP2 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The overall Spearman's correlation between Gdf11 and Mecp2 across all cell types in the normal mouse brain was 0.65.
source: We mined a previous single-nucleus RNA-sequencing experiment in the normal mouse brain and found that the overall Spearman's correlation between Gdf11 and Mecp2 across all cell types was 0.65 (Saunders et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of data from Saunders et al., 2018, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Gdf11 and Mecp2 were highly correlated in neuronal and glial cell types (astrocytes, microglia, neurons, and oligodendrocytes; Spearman's rho = 0.6–0.92).
source: Further, Gdf11 and Mecp2 were highly correlated in neuronal and glial cell types (astrocytes, microglia, neurons, and oligodendrocytes; Spearman's rho = 0.6–0.92) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Gdf11 and Mecp2 were highly correlated in excitatory neurons (Spearman's rho = 0.65).
source: Within neurons specifically, we found that Gdf11 and Mecp2 were highly correlated in both excitatory neurons (Spearman's rho = 0.65) and inhibitory neurons (Spearman's rho = 0.76) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Gdf11 and Mecp2 were highly correlated in inhibitory neurons (Spearman's rho = 0.76).
source: Within neurons specifically, we found that Gdf11 and Mecp2 were highly correlated in both excitatory neurons (Spearman's rho = 0.65) and inhibitory neurons (Spearman's rho = 0.76) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Gdf11 is sensitive to MeCP2 levels.
source: Given the strong dynamic correlation of Gdf11 with MeCP2 levels upon ASO treatment and with Mecp2 expression in individual brain cell types (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F), these data suggest Gdf11 is also sensitive to MeCP2 levels.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the correlation data presented in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: The expression of Mecp2 was not changed by reduction of Gdf11.
source: The expression of Mecp2 was not changed by reduction of Gdf11, but Gdf11 was significantly decreased in Mecp2-knockout males (p<0.05) and increased in MECP2-TG1 animals (p<0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Gdf11 was significantly decreased in Mecp2-knockout males (p<0.05).
source: The expression of Mecp2 was not changed by reduction of Gdf11, but Gdf11 was significantly decreased in Mecp2-knockout males (p<0.05) and increased in MECP2-TG1 animals (p<0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Gdf11 was significantly increased in MECP2-TG1 animals (p<0.0001).
source: The expression of Mecp2 was not changed by reduction of Gdf11, but Gdf11 was significantly decreased in Mecp2-knockout males (p<0.05) and increased in MECP2-TG1 animals (p<0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Mecp2-knockout trended towards a further decrease of Gdf11 in the Mecp2-/y; Gdf11tm2b/+ double mutants.
source: Furthermore, Mecp2-knockout trended towards a further decrease of Gdf11 in the Mecp2-/y; Gdf11tm2b/+ double mutants while Gdf11 was restored to wild-type expression in the MECP2-TG1; Gdf11tm2b/+ double mutants.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Gdf11 was restored to wild-type expression in the MECP2-TG1; Gdf11tm2b/+ double mutants.
source: Furthermore, Mecp2-knockout trended towards a further decrease of Gdf11 in the Mecp2-/y; Gdf11tm2b/+ double mutants while Gdf11 was restored to wild-type expression in the MECP2-TG1; Gdf11tm2b/+ double mutants.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of the LacZ reporter was significantly downregulated in Mecp2-knockout (p<0.05).
source: Last, expression of the LacZ reporter was modulated by MeCP2 levels as well, being significantly downregulated in Mecp2-knockout (p<0.05) and upregulated in MECP2-TG1 animals (p<0.05) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of the LacZ reporter was upregulated in MECP2-TG1 animals (p<0.05).
source: Last, expression of the LacZ reporter was modulated by MeCP2 levels as well, being significantly downregulated in Mecp2-knockout (p<0.05) and upregulated in MECP2-TG1 animals (p<0.05) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The Gdf11 locus is transcriptionally sensitive to MeCP2 protein levels.
source: These results demonstrate that the Gdf11 locus is transcriptionally sensitive to MeCP2 protein levels.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the qPCR and LacZ reporter data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: MeCP2 loss has been shown to cause a down-regulation of gene expression.
source: While MeCP2 has a well-described role as a transcriptional repressor and its loss leads to a de-repression of gene expression, MeCP2 loss has been shown to cause a down-regulation of gene expression (Ben-Shachar et al., 2009; Boxer et al., 2020; Chahrour et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2015; Clemens et al., 2020; Lyst et al., 2013; Nan et al., 1998; Nan et al., 1997; Samaco et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A peak of MeCP2 binding was identified upstream of the Gdf11 transcriptional start site.
source: We next identified peaks of enriched binding using the MACS algorithm (Zhang et al., 2008), which identified a peak upstream of the Gdf11 transcriptional start site (TSS).
evidence: This is supported by CUT&RUN data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The peak of MeCP2 signal coincided with a region of high H3K27ac and H3K4me1, but low H3K4me3, suggesting that MeCP2 binds a putative enhancer of Gdf11.
source: The peak of MeCP2 signal coincided with a region of high H3K27ac and H3K4me1, but low H3K4me3, suggesting that MeCP2 binds a putative enhancer of Gdf11 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is an inference based on histone modification patterns shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: There was a significant (p<0.01) increase of MeCP2 binding within the region upstream of Gdf11 in the MECP2-TG1 hippocampus.
source: We observed a significant (p<0.01) increase of MeCP2 binding within this region upstream of Gdf11 in the MECP2-TG1 hippocampus.
evidence: This is supported by CUT&RUN data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The MeCP2 binding signal was almost completely absent in the Mecp2-knockout hippocampus in the region upstream of Gdf11.
source: Importantly, the MeCP2 binding signal was almost completely absent in the Mecp2-knockout hippocampus in this same region (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by CUT&RUN data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: H3K27me3 has been shown to interact with and be modulated by MeCP2.
source: Concurrently, we profiled the repressive histone modification H3K27me3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C), which has been shown to interact with and be modulated by MeCP2 (Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020.

claim: There was a significant (p<0.01) increase in H3K27me3 occupancy in Mecp2-knockout tissue within the window of MeCP2 binding upstream of Gdf11.
source: Within the window of MeCP2 binding upstream of Gdf11, we found a significant (p<0.01) increase in H3K27me3 occupancy in Mecp2-knockout tissue and a trend towards a reciprocal decrease in H3K27me3 occupancy in MECP2-TG1 tissue (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by CUT&RUN data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: There was a trend towards a reciprocal decrease in H3K27me3 occupancy in MECP2-TG1 tissue within the window of MeCP2 binding upstream of Gdf11.
source: Within the window of MeCP2 binding upstream of Gdf11, we found a significant (p<0.01) increase in H3K27me3 occupancy in Mecp2-knockout tissue and a trend towards a reciprocal decrease in H3K27me3 occupancy in MECP2-TG1 tissue (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by CUT&RUN data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The increase in H3K27me3 in Mecp2-knockout tissue corroborates the downregulation observed in Gdf11 expression in transcriptional profiles collected from Mecp2-deficient models.
source: The increase in H3K27me3 in Mecp2-knockout tissue corroborates the downregulation we observe in Gdf11 expression in transcriptional profiles collected from Mecp2-deficient models (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an inference connecting the H3K27me3 data to the expression data.

claim: MeCP2 binds upstream of Gdf11, at a putative enhancer, and modifies the chromatin landscape around the Gdf11 locus to regulate Gdf11 expression.
source: These results suggest that MeCP2 binds upstream of Gdf11, at a putative enhancer, and modifies the chromatin landscape around the Gdf11 locus to regulate Gdf11 expression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the CUT&RUN data showing MeCP2 binding and H3K27me3 changes.

claim: MECP2-TG1 mice are hypoactive when placed in an open arena, traveling less distance, and exhibiting fewer horizontal and vertical exploratory activities compared to wild-type mice.
source: Compared to wild-type mice, MECP2-TG1 mice are hypoactive when placed in an open arena, traveling less distance, and exhibiting fewer horizontal and vertical exploratory activities (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Normalizing Gdf11 expression in the double mutant mice resulted in rescue of total distance traveled and horizontal activity.
source: Normalizing Gdf11 expression in the double mutant mice resulted in rescue of total distance traveled and horizontal activity.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A partial rescue of vertical exploration was observed in MECP2-TG1; Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.
source: We also observed a partial rescue of vertical exploration and an improvement in anxiety-like behavior in the open arena as assessed by entries into the center (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: An improvement in anxiety-like behavior in the open arena as assessed by entries into the center was observed in MECP2-TG1; Gdf11tm2b/+ mice.
source: We also observed a partial rescue of vertical exploration and an improvement in anxiety-like behavior in the open arena as assessed by entries into the center (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MECP2-TG1 mice experience hypoactivity and anxiety-like behavior compared to wild-type mice when placed in an elevated plus maze apparatus, traveling less distance and entering the open arms fewer times.
source: Next, MECP2-TG1 mice experience hypoactivity and anxiety-like behavior compared to wild-type mice when placed in an elevated plus maze apparatus, traveling less distance and entering the open arms fewer times.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The double mutant animals entered the open arms and crossed the maze arms like wild-type animals.
source: In contrast, we observed the double mutant animals entered the open arms and crossed the maze arms like wild-type animals, and the double mutant mice traveled significantly further (p<0.01) on the maze compared to MECP2-TG1 mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The double mutant mice traveled significantly further (p<0.01) on the maze compared to MECP2-TG1 mice.
source: In contrast, we observed the double mutant animals entered the open arms and crossed the maze arms like wild-type animals, and the double mutant mice traveled significantly further (p<0.01) on the maze compared to MECP2-TG1 mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: MECP2-TG1 mice exhibit improved learning compared to wild-type mice in a shock-tone cued fear paradigm.
source: Lastly, MECP2-TG1 mice exhibit improved learning compared to wild-type mice in a shock-tone cued fear paradigm.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MECP2-TG1 mice freeze more in both context and cued tests in a shock-tone cued fear paradigm.
source: Specifically, mice are trained to associate a tone with a foot shock and then placed in the same environment without tone (context) or a new environment with a tone (cue). Learning in this assay is measured by the amount of time the mouse freezes, where MECP2-TG1 mice freeze more in both context and cued tests.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and Figure 2C.

claim: Normalization of Gdf11 led to wild-type levels of freezing during the training routine.
source: Normalization of Gdf11 led to wild-type levels of freezing during the training routine, and normalized the cued learning compared to MECP2-TG1 mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Normalization of Gdf11 normalized the cued learning compared to MECP2-TG1 mice.
source: Normalization of Gdf11 led to wild-type levels of freezing during the training routine, and normalized the cued learning compared to MECP2-TG1 mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Contextual learning was improved in double mutant mice with no significant difference observed compared to wild-type mice.
source: Contextual learning was improved in double mutant mice with no significant difference observed compared to wild-type mice (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Reduction of Gdf11 did not rescue motor coordination on the rotating rod in MECP2-TG1 mice.
source: Reduction of Gdf11 did not rescue all phenotypes present in MECP2-TG1 mice, as we did not observe a rescue in motor coordination on the rotating rod, change in the time spent in dark during the light-dark assay, nor any changes in sociability.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Reduction of Gdf11 did not rescue the time spent in dark during the light-dark assay in MECP2-TG1 mice.
source: Reduction of Gdf11 did not rescue all phenotypes present in MECP2-TG1 mice, as we did not observe a rescue in motor coordination on the rotating rod, change in the time spent in dark during the light-dark assay, nor any changes in sociability.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Reduction of Gdf11 did not rescue sociability in MECP2-TG1 mice.
source: Reduction of Gdf11 did not rescue all phenotypes present in MECP2-TG1 mice, as we did not observe a rescue in motor coordination on the rotating rod, change in the time spent in dark during the light-dark assay, nor any changes in sociability.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F-G.
